analyst_observations: With-skill passes all assertions; baseline fails one per eval (identity sentence process step in eval 1, invention labeling in eval 3).
Both failed baseline assertions test skill-specific process behaviors (identity sentence, invention labeling) — these are discriminating assertions that measure skill adherence, not general quality.

Content quality is close between variants. The baseline produces solid faction pages thanks to the template being well-structured. The skill's value-add is in process discipline (identity sentence, invention gates) and craft guidance (pressure-forward DM thesis, collision mapping).
With-skill uses ~17% more tokens and ~57% more time. The extra cost buys the process steps and reference file consultation. Acceptable for a design skill.

The DM thesis quality difference is qualitative: with-skill produces more pressure-forward theses ('doctrine cracks as the Maw escalates') vs baseline's summary-style ('doctrine of non-intervention turns observation into vulnerability'). Both are usable.
